title: Find the Longest Semi-Repetitive Substring
summary: Given a digit string s, find the longest substring where there is at most one adjacent pair of the same digit.
statement: Given a digit string s, find the longest substring where there is at most one adjacent pair of the same digit. For example, '0010', '0123', and '54944' are valid, but '00101022' and '1101234883' are not.
constraints: A substring is semi-repetitive when it contains at most one adjacent equal-digit pair.
Pairs may overlap; for example, 111 contains two equal adjacent pairs.
Return the maximum length of a semi-repetitive substring.
hints: A valid sliding window may contain zero or one equal-adjacent boundary.
Remember the right index of the most recent equal pair.
When a new equal pair appears, move left just after the previous pair’s left character, then remember the new pair.
This removes exactly the oldest forbidden pair while retaining the longest suffix that contains at most the newest one.
editorial: This removes exactly the oldest forbidden pair while retaining the longest suffix that contains at most the newest one.

tests.explanation: The substring 5223 has only the pair 22 and length four; including the final 3 creates a second pair.
No adjacent digits match, so the entire string of length four qualifies.
